subject: c12-chem
note: Official CBSE Class XII Chemistry theory paper: 70 marks. The 2026-27 course structure assigns marks directly to the ten listed units; practical is separate.
mistakes: Solutions: confusing molarity and molality or using temperature-dependent concentration units in a temperature-sensitive context.
Solutions: applying colligative-property relations without checking the van't Hoff factor or abnormal-molar-mass condition.
Electrochemistry: reversing anode/cathode or oxidation/reduction signs when moving between galvanic and electrolytic cells.
Electrochemistry: using the Nernst equation with an incorrect reaction quotient or inconsistent logarithm convention.
Chemical Kinetics: mixing zero-order and first-order integrated equations and half-life relations.
Chemical Kinetics: confusing rate constant units with reaction rate units.
d- and f-Block: memorising trends without distinguishing general transition-metal behaviour from specific exceptions and compounds.
Coordination Compounds: losing track of ligand names, coordination number, oxidation state, geometry and isomerism while naming a complex.
Organic Chemistry: writing a reaction without checking the reagent, condition, substrate class and major product.
Amines: confusing basicity trends and chemical properties, or mixing diazotisation and coupling conditions.
Biomolecules: memorising classifications without connecting monomers, linkages, functions and examples.
order: Do Solutions, Electrochemistry and Chemical Kinetics first; practise their numerical patterns immediately after learning each concept.
Study d- and f-Block with a compact trend/compound sheet and revise it repeatedly rather than cramming once.
Complete Coordination Compounds next, especially terminology, nomenclature, isomerism and bonding.
Study the organic sequence in order: Haloalkanes and Haloarenes → Alcohols, Phenols and Ethers → Aldehydes, Ketones and Carboxylic Acids → Amines.
Finish Biomolecules with linked tables for carbohydrates, proteins, enzymes, vitamins, nucleic acids and hormones.
After the first complete pass, practise mixed conversion/reaction questions and numerical questions together.
Use the official sample paper and marking scheme to check answer style and coverage.

reference.label: Solutions
reference.text: Revise types of solutions; concentration expressions; solubility; vapour pressure; ideal and non-ideal solutions; colligative properties and molar-mass determination; abnormal molecular masses.

reference.label: Electrochemistry
reference.text: Revise electrochemical and galvanic cells; Nernst equation; conductance of electrolytic solutions; electrolytic cells and electrolysis; batteries; fuel cells; corrosion.

reference.label: Chemical Kinetics
reference.text: Revise rate of reaction; factors affecting rate; integrated rate equations; temperature dependence of reaction rate; collision theory of chemical reactions.

reference.label: d- and f-Block Elements
reference.text: Revise periodic position and electronic configuration; general properties of transition elements; important transition-metal compounds; lanthanoids; actinoids; applications of d- and f-block elements.

reference.label: Coordination Compounds
reference.text: Revise Werner’s theory; important coordination terminology; nomenclature; isomerism; bonding in coordination compounds; bonding in metal carbonyls; importance and applications.

reference.label: Haloalkanes and Haloarenes
reference.text: Revise classification, nomenclature, C–X bond, preparation, physical properties, chemical reactions and polyhalogen compounds of haloalkanes/haloarenes.

reference.label: Alcohols, Phenols and Ethers
reference.text: Revise classification, nomenclature, functional-group structures, alcohols, phenols, commercially important alcohols and ethers.

reference.label: Aldehydes, Ketones and Carboxylic Acids
reference.text: Revise carbonyl-group nomenclature and structure; preparation, physical properties, chemical reactions and uses of aldehydes/ketones; carboxyl-group nomenclature and structure; preparation, physical properties, chemical reactions and uses of carboxylic acids.

reference.label: Amines
reference.text: Revise structure, classification, nomenclature and preparation of amines; physical and chemical properties; preparation and reactions of diazonium salts; importance of diazonium salts in synthesis of aromatic compounds.

reference.label: Biomolecules
reference.text: Revise carbohydrates, proteins, enzymes, vitamins, nucleic acids and hormones.

certification_note: Audited against the CBSE Class XII Chemistry 2026-27 theory course structure. Theory paper scope only; practical work is excluded. Weightage is preserved from the source file. Quick-reference coverage follows the ten prescribed theory units and does not add separately listed formative-only topics to the summative preparation reference.
